title: Cliff-face Wang autotiling — cliff faces resolve their variant per neighbouring cliffs at same height level
intent: GDP-2026-05-28-010 (variable height) ships cliffs as PLAIN side faces — a vertical stripe shader uniform. When two adjacent cells both have height (e.g. row of H=2 cells next to a row of H=0 cells), the cliff face between them renders as separate undifferentiated strips per cell — no autotiling. Cliffs read as 'a row of unconnected stair-step boxes', not 'a continuous wall'. This story makes cliff faces ALSO autotile via the Wang engine module — neighbouring cliffs at the same height-level share a Wang bitmask, and cliff face geometry varies per bitmask (sharp corner at cliff-edge, smooth continuation in the middle, end-cap where cliff terminates). Cliff faces ALSO get biome-specific styles per the family from GDP-2026-05-29-005 — stone cliff has bevels, dirt cliff is crumbled, grass cliff has overhanging roots, etc.
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-29 — 'утесы тоже стыковались между собой'. Audit of `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/floor-cell-builder.ts` or similar (cliff faces come from variable-height cuboid generation in GDP-010) confirms cliff faces are plain side material — no Wang autotile. After GDP-2026-05-29-004 (Wang rotation) + GDP-2026-05-29-005 (biome geometry) ship, the floor + walls look 'organic + connected', but cliffs still look 'step-block stair'. This is the last visible 'набор кубов' surface.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: GDP-2026-05-28-010 (variable cell height — cliffs exist). GDP-2026-05-29-004 (Wang rotation pattern established). GDP-2026-05-29-005 (per-biome geometry styles).

CONCEPT: cliffs are NOT cell entities — they're EDGES between cells with height delta > 0 (per GDP-010 CliffComputeSystem). To autotile cliff faces, treat each cliff EDGE as a Wang tile entity, compute its bitmask from neighbouring cliff edges at the same height-level.
CLIFF WANG FAMILY (new family registered alongside floor families):
Family name: 'cliff-face' (or 'cliff-{biome}' per biome, see below).
Wang bitmask: at each cliff edge, check 4 'cardinal-cliff-neighbours' — does an adjacent cliff EDGE exist at the same height-level?
N-cliff-neighbour: is there a cliff edge directly NORTH (same X axis, +1 Y) at same heightTop?
E-cliff-neighbour: same height-top E.
S, W: same.
16 bitmasks → 16 (or 16→5 with rotation per GDP-2026-05-29-004 pattern) cliff face variants.

Edge types: 'corner cliff' (vertical edge), 'straight cliff' (long horizontal wall), 'isolated cliff' (single column), 'cliff-end-cap' (where cliff terminates at an arena boundary or a non-cliff cell).
CLIFF FACE GEOMETRIES (5 procedural builders, biome-specific):
Variant 0 (edge / single-side cliff) — vertical face with edge-detail trim on the open side (looks like 'wall end').
Variant 1 (cliff corner — two adjacent cliff edges meet at a 90° angle) — corner face with the corner-vertical-edge highlighted.
Variant 2 (filler — surrounded by other cliffs) — flat vertical face with biome-style detail (panel seam for stone, irregular crumble for dirt, etc.).
Variant 3 (isolated cliff column — single column of height) — narrow vertical column with rounded edges.
Variant 4 (straight cliff wall — both sides continue) — long flat vertical face with seams or detail.
BIOME-SPECIFIC CLIFF FACE STYLES:

cliff-grass: face is brown-dirt at bottom, transitioning to GREEN with overhanging grass tufts at the top edge (the cliff-top has grass texture continuing over the edge). Visual: 'cliff with grassy hilltop'.
cliff-path: smoothly-curved face, soft slope.
cliff-stone: sharp beveled face with vertical column seam (granite-block feel).
cliff-dirt: irregular vertical face with crumble texture (vertex displacement).
cliff-floor (industrial/lab): flat panelled face with horizontal seam lines.
Biome selected automatically from the TOP cell's FloorTerrain family — a cliff under a grass cell uses 'cliff-grass' style.
INTEGRATION WITH HEIGHT (GDP-010):
CliffComputeSystem (existing) marks cliff edges. NEW: a CliffFaceWangResolverSystem then iterates cliff edge entities, computes bitmask per the cliff-Wang family, writes variant + rotation.
Cliff face mesh entity spawned per cliff edge (replaces the current single-cuboid side-face approach from GDP-010).
Each cliff face: one Mesh entity, child of the cliff edge entity. Visual stitches with neighbours.
MULTIPLE-HEIGHT-CLIFF-COLUMNS:
When a cell at H=3 sits next to a cell at H=0, the cliff has 3 rows of cliff face (H=0→1, H=1→2, H=2→3). Each row gets its own Wang resolution.

Top row's biome = TOP cell's biome (e.g. grass). Bottom rows could use TOP cell's biome OR cycle through 'stratified' biomes (e.g. top=grass, middle=dirt, bottom=stone). Stratified = more natural; pick this for v1.

Stratification rule: top-to-bottom biome priority — first row uses cell's TOP biome; deeper rows pick from the per-theme stratification table (warehouse theme: top=floor, mid=floor, bottom=stone; lab theme: top=floor all the way; grass theme arena: top=grass, mid=dirt, bottom=stone).
ROUNDED CLIFF-TOP EDGE:
Cliff TOP face (where the floor meets the cliff edge) — small chamfer / radius on the top edge so it doesn't look like a sharp 90° step.
Implementation: in the cliff face mesh, top vertices inset slightly inward + add a chamfer face. Or use a bevel modifier per family.
BIOME-SPECIFIC OVERHANG (organic touch):
cliff-grass top edge: small overhang of grass blades (the grass extends ~0.05 cells out from the cliff edge, falls forward — like a hillside).
cliff-dirt top edge: irregular overhang.
cliff-stone / cliff-path: flat top edge (no overhang — geometric).
cliff-floor: small panel seam at the top edge.
~50 LOC additional per biome.
BACKWARDS COMPATIBILITY:
Pre-this-story cliff face: plain shader-painted side. After: Wang-resolved per cliff edge.
Existing arena with heightmaps (cliffside.scene.json from GDP-010) renders with proper cliff face autotiling.
PERFORMANCE:
Per cliff edge: 1 mesh entity vs 1 cuboid side face today — about equal entity count. Wang resolver runs once per cliff edge at scene-load + on height-change events.

Cliff face geometry slightly more complex than plain box side (chamfered edges, biome overhangs) — ~200 vertices per face vs ~10 today. At 50 cliff edges in a tall arena = ~10000 extra vertices. Within budget.
MULTIPLAYER: cliff edges deterministic from height + biome data; both server + client recompute. No protocol changes.
TESTS:
Cliff edge entity gets Wang bitmask + variant + rotation.
3 adjacent cliff edges on a straight wall: middle uses variant 4 (straight) + biome-specific style; ends use variant 0 (edge) + rotated outward.
Cliff under grass cell uses cliff-grass biome face; cliff under stone cell uses cliff-stone.
Multi-row cliff (3 rows): top row uses TOP biome, lower rows use stratified biomes per theme.
Rounded chamfer at cliff top.
VISUAL QA:

Load `cliffside.scene.json` (3×3 plateau at H=2 in middle of arena) → cliff faces around plateau visibly connect; corners look like corners, straight edges look like flat walls, isolated cliff columns get end-caps.
Plateau has grass on top → cliff face shows grass-overhang at top transitioning to dirt-and-stone biome rows below.
Walking around the plateau, the cliff doesn't feel 'stepped' — feels like a continuous geological feature.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Curved cliffs (non-straight wall sections). 4-cardinal cliff edges only.
Vegetation / props on cliff faces (vines, moss patches). Static geometry only.
Animated cliff erosion (cliff face changes over rounds). Static.
Cliff faces affected by blasts (charred cliff face). Blasts don't damage cliff faces in current rules.
Player-paintable cliff biome. Authored / computed only.
Cliff-face decals (mentioned in GDP-2026-05-29-001 as out-of-scope there). Same — out here too.
